noveltyJustification: All six findings are new: the direct pre-fix validator run, the name-only required-section check, the numbered-only H2 regex, the unenforced related placement, the absent content checks and the setext-rewarding divider rule.
answeredQuestions: Why do the sk-doc templates, authoring guidance and validate_document.py fail to detect each defect class, traced check by check?
ruledOut: Validator disabled for the tested paths

label: The pre-fix web-cascade file and four current defective files each return valid true with total_issues 0 under --type reference, confirming the validator gap by execution.
Required sections are matched by heading name and substring only, so OVERVIEW AND CASCADE AND SPECIFICITY satisfies requiredSections overview even with no overview prose.
The H2 checker matches only numbered digits-dot headings, so 2b and unnumbered H2s are invisible, and non-sequential numbers are warnings rather than blocking errors.
recommendedSections is only read inside the router branch, so related_resources is never required or ordered for references; the rule data also contradicts the asset template must-be-last clause.

The validator has no content-level checks for adjacent bold labels, setext hazards, bare URLs, duplicated content, intro length or item order; orchestration runs only TOC, H2, structure, required sections and frontmatter.

The divider rule requires a horizontal rule above numbered H2s but never a blank line above that rule, so the setext-producing layout passes; the template duplicated when-to-create guidance compounds the gap.
